{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1792975145176,"sessionID":"ses_e8a5ccbdeffeNdzc6hS4oyrN0k","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_011rKfEuegBgFv4PMdMXCxGp","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r1/matmul/matmul.cpp","content":"// Hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA matrix multiplication benchmark.\n//\n// Decomposition:\n//   - MPI:    C is split into contiguous row blocks, one per rank. Every rank\n//             generates A and B locally (deterministic), so no input traffic.\n//   - OpenMP: within a rank, one thread drives the local GPU while the other\n//             threads run CPU workers. All of them pull row chunks from a\n//             shared atomic scheduler, so the faster device automatically\n//             takes more of the work.\n//   - CUDA:   shared-memory tiled GEMM with per-thread register blocking.\n//\n// Numerical semantics: every element C[i][j] is accumulated as\n//     sum = 0; for k = 0..N-1: sum += A[i][k] * B[k][j]\n// in strictly increasing k, exactly like the reference loop, on both the CPU\n// and the GPU path. Results are therefore bit-identical to the serial code\n// (given FMA contraction, which both gcc -march=native and nvcc -fmad=true\n// apply to this expression).\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <omp.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <atomic>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <climits>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nnamespace {\n\n// Work-distribution granularity (rows of C).\nconstexpr size_t GPU_CHUNK_ROWS = 128;\nconstexpr size_t CPU_CHUNK_ROWS = 16;\n\n// CPU micro-kernel blocking.\nconstexpr size_t CPU_ROW_BLOCK = 8;\nconstexpr size_t CPU_COL_TILE = 512;\n\n// GPU tiled kernel: 64x64 output tile per block, 16x16 threads, 4x4 per thread.\nconstexpr int GEMM_BM = 64;\nconstexpr int GEMM_BN = 64;\nconstexpr int GEMM_BK = 16;\nconstexpr int GEMM_TM = 4;\nconstexpr int GEMM_TN = 4;\nconstexpr int GEMM_THREADS = 256;\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                          \\\n    do {                                                                          \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,      \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_)); {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1792975153603,"sessionID":"ses_e8a5ccbdeffeNdzc6hS4oyrN0k","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01MXoCPCW7UAsNLSkcFCkU3e","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r1/matmul/CMakeLists.txt","content":"cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.18)\nproject(matmul_benchmark LANGUAGES CXX CUDA)\n\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\n\n# Default GPU architectures (Volta through Hopper); override with\n# -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=<list> for a specific cluster.\nif(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)\n    set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES 70 75 80 86 89 90)\nendif()\n\nfind_package(MPI REQUIRED)\nfind_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)\nfind_package(CUDAToolkit REQUIRED)\n\n# The CUDA kernels live in matmul.cpp, so compile that file with nvcc.\nset_source_files_properties(matmul.cpp PROPERTIES LANGUAGE CUDA)\n\nadd_executable(matmul matmul.cpp)\n\ntarget_compile_options(matmul PRIVATE\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:-O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-O3 -fmad=true\n        -Xcompiler=-march=native -Xcompiler=-Wall -Xcompiler=-Wextra\n        -Xcompiler=-fopenmp -Xcompiler=-ffp-contract=fast>\n)\n\ntarget_link_libraries(matmul PRIVATE\n    MPI::MPI_CXX\n    OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX\n    CUDA::cudart\n    m\n)\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r1/matmul/CMakeLists.txt","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r1/matmul/CMakeLists.txt","time":{"start":1792975153553,"end":1792975153562}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_175a5a0770013hUKgvrETbnDBb","sessionID":"ses_e8a5ccbdeffeNdzc6hS4oyrN0k","messageID":"msg_175a59c04001Jc4HOjoO3OlTEQ"}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1792975342439,"sessionID":"ses_e8a5ccbdeffeNdzc6hS4oyrN0k","part":{"id":"prt_175a868e40013HlOzQBWn3QVQA","messageID":"msg_175a86524001uG4LiGvmInoYjl","sessionID":"ses_e8a5ccbdeffeNdzc6hS4oyrN0k","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm realizing the reference implementation's behavior around floating-point contraction isn't actually deterministic—it depends on the compiler's choices about which loops get fused multiply-add treatment, since reduction loops can't be vectorized without reassociation flags.\n\nGiven that, exact bit-matching across all N isn't something the reference itself guarantees, so I should treat validation as a tolerance check (1e-6 relative) rather than demanding bitwise equality—I'll aim to get as close as possible but be upfront that matching a compiler-dependent mix exactly isn't realistic. I should also check whether the CPU and GPU paths at least agree with each other when both use the same fusion strategy.\n\nThe more important goal is determinism: results shouldn't vary depending on which device computed a given row, so I want to make sure CPU and GPU paths use matching fused-multiply-add arithmetic, possibly setting explicit fast-contraction flags for the CPU build to match the GPU's fmad=true behavior. I'd verify this by comparing outputs at a small N against a known fused reference value.\n\nTo test bit-for-bit equality between CPU and GPU execution, I'm planning scratch copies of the matmul code with one variant forcing GPU to handle everything and another forcing CPU-only execution by tweaking the thread-dispatch condition so only the CPU worker path runs.\n\n","time":{"start":1792975333604,"end":1792975342379},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1792975342440,"sessionID":"ses_e8a5ccbdeffeNdzc6hS4oyrN0k","part":{"id":"prt_175a88b2f0015MUHd93Y64ItcY","messageID":"msg_175a86524001uG4LiGvmInoYjl","sessionID":"ses_e8a5ccbdeffeNdzc6hS4oyrN0k","type":"text","text":"The reference is not self-consistent: `-ffp-contract=off` changes its output for some sizes (N=5, 17, 129) and not others, so the original's bits depend on how GCC happened to vectorize. Bit-identity with the original across all sizes is therefore not achievable as a general guarantee. The tolerance-based validation is the real correctness bar. The property I can and should guarantee is that the CPU and GPU paths agree with each other, so results don't depend on which device computed a row. I'll test that by building CPU-only and GPU-only variants in scratch.","time":{"start":1792975342383,"end":1792975342397}}}
